verdict.rationale: Capacities documents itself as an offline-first app: you can work offline, changes sync when you reconnect, search works offline, and media can be downloaded for offline viewing. Ownership and readability without the app come only through its own exports. Scheduled full exports produce human- and machine-readable Markdown with front matter plus CSV, but the primary store is not a set of local files you own. Missing for 10: notes stored natively as local files or a user-owned local store readable without the app (rather than via periodic exports), confirmation that every feature works fully offline, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, my notes live in local files or a local-first store that I own and can read without the app, and everything keeps working fully offline

citations.quote: Capacities is an offline-first application. You can work offline and your changes will get synchronized as soon as you're back online.
It works offline on all devices, giving you quick search results every time.
Capacities can also download all media files to your device so that they load faster and you can view them offline.
You can schedule automatic exports by going to `Settings > Full Export > Automated Full Export > Add Schedule`.
Exports from Capacities are fully human- and machine-readable at the same time.
